ordered_diagnoses: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Connective Tissue Disease

s1.syndrome_frame: a middle-aged woman with progressive dyspnea, polyarthritis, joint swelling, and Raynaud's phenomenon, with evidence of pulmonary hypertension and abnormal laboratory studies
salient_findings: elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and antinuclear antibody titer
pulmonary hypertension with elevated pulmonary arterial systolic pressure
key_facts: 2-month history of fatigue, weakness, polyarthritis, and joint swelling
9 months earlier diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary hypertension
elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 45 mm/h
negative tests for anti-Scl-70, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C virus, and rheumatoid arthritis
effusion of multiple metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints
Raynaud's phenomenon elicited by cold-water immersion
elevated pulmonary arterial systolic pressure of 80 mm Hg
mild mitral regurgitation and moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation

shortlist: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Connective Tissue Disease

shortlist.label: Systemic Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of Raynaud's phenomenon, polyarthritis, joint swelling, and elevated anti-centromere antibody level

shortlist.label: Limited Systemic Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated anti-centromere antibody level and presence of pulmonary hypertension

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of symptoms from multiple connective tissue diseases, including polyarthritis and pulmonary hypertension

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of pulmonary hypertension and connective tissue disease symptoms

shortlist.label: CREST Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of Calcinosis, Raynaud's phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasia, which are all consistent with the patient's symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of anti-centromere antibodies, Raynaud's phenomenon, and pulmonary hypertension are characteristic of limited systemic sclerosis, which is also known as CREST syndrome. The patient's symptoms and laboratory results, including the high anti-centromere antibody level and the absence of anti-Scl-70 antibodies, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Systemic Sclerosis
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of systemic sclerosis, the absence of skin thickening and the presence of anti-centromere antibodies suggest limited systemic sclerosis is a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not meet the criteria for mixed connective tissue disease, which typically includes a combination of features from multiple connective tissue diseases.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: This diagnosis is too broad and does not capture the specific features of the patient's disease, including the presence of anti-centromere antibodies and Raynaud's phenomenon.

rejected.label: CREST Syndrome
rejected.why: CREST syndrome is another name for limited systemic sclerosis, so it is not a distinct diagnosis from the champion.
